objective: Provide the explicit repository-side review/check policy required by safe auto-merge, with human-approved settings and a verified receipt.
acceptanceCriteria:
Approved dev policy requires effective CI, independent fresh review and resolved conversations, with no automatic bypass.
Auto-merge is enabled only after explicit settings approval and verified review availability.
A failing/unreviewed test PR cannot merge; a compliant PR is eligible for the normal merge path.
Before/after configuration and reviewer constraints are recorded without secrets.
nonGoals: No source implementation, broad organization policies, direct merge, bypass grant or unapproved settings write.
risks: risk:high: Proposed policy: enable repository auto-merge; protect dev using the repository's supported rule mechanism; require one independent approving review, dismiss stale approvals after code pushes, resolve conversations, require current ubuntu/windows Factory CI checks and prohibit agent/admin bypass. Resolve actual effective check contexts from a fresh CI run rather than assume names from display text. PR #24 passed test (ubuntu-latest) and test (windows-latest), but the configured names must be verified. A human repository administrator must approve the exact settings diff, reviewer availability and bypass policy before any write. This issue does not authorize applying settings. Record before/after effective policy and confirm checks apply to dev; a same-author agent cannot substitute for the required independent reviewer. If unavailable, leave merge blocked.
suggestedWorkBreakdown:
Capture effective current rules/settings and propose the exact minimal configuration using observed required CI contexts.
Obtain explicit human plan approval covering repository settings and independent-review arrangement.
Apply only approved settings through the supported GitHub interface; verify effective enforcement using a non-production test PR without bypassing checks.
Record the gate-policy receipt and link it to the current-head merge-gate implementation.
unresolvedQuestions: Awaiting explicit human approval of the recorded high-risk plan.
